name: scenario_Palettes_a_script_drives_the_effects
description: A palette written as a MoonLive script, end to end: the file lands on the device, the picker offers it by name, it compiles and puts its own control on the Drivers card, every effect samples what it computes each frame, and a control turned on the card reaches the script. The scenario removes its file afterwards, so the device's picker is left as it was found.

reset.name: reset-palette
reset.description: A built-in, so the scenario starts from a palette that needs no script.

fixture.name: grid
fixture.description: A 16x16 panel, small enough to run anywhere.

fixture.name: effect
fixture.description: An effect that samples the palette for every light, so the script's colors are what it paints.

steps.name: write-the-palette
steps.description: A palette script as a user would save it: one control, and sixteen entries computed from it every frame.

steps.name: pick-it-by-name
steps.description: By name, since a scripted palette's index moves as files come and go.

steps.name: its-control-is-on-the-card
steps.description: Only a compiled script publishes its controls, so this proves the compile as well.

steps.name: measure-scripted
steps.description: The frame cost with the script computing the palette, which is independent of the rig's size.

steps.name: restart
steps.description: A scripted palette chosen by name must come back running, not only listed.

steps.name: the-script-came-back
steps.description: Its control exists only while its script runs, so this proves the script reattached after the restart.

steps.name: back-to-a-built-in
steps.description: Detach the script before its file goes, as a user switching palettes would.

steps.name: remove-the-palette
steps.description: Leave the device's picker as it was found.

steps.name: still-rendering
steps.description: The effects keep painting with the file gone.
